_sources.pluto: NASA NSSDCA Pluto fact sheet; JPL SSD
_sources.eris: Sicardy et al. 2011 (radius, albedo); Holler et al. 2021 (mass, density); Szakats et al. 2023 (rotation)
_sources.haumea: Ortiz et al. 2017 (triaxial shape, density, albedo)
_sources.makemake: Ortiz et al. 2012 (radius); Parker et al. 2018 (mass); Heinze & de Lahunta 2015 (rotation)

temperature.note: NSSDCA Small Worlds mean (-225 C); surface range ~33-55 K

pluto.summary: Pluto is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt with a nitrogen-dominated atmosphere, visited by New Horizons in July 2015. Pluto and its largest moon Charon orbit a barycentre outside Pluto.

temperature.note: approximate mean surface temperature (30-56 K range); poorly constrained

discovery.by: Brown, M. E., Trujillo, C. A., Rabinowitz, D. (discovery images 2003-10-21; identified 2005-01-05)

eris.summary: Eris is the most massive known dwarf planet, a scattered-disc object about as large as Pluto. Its discovery in 2005 helped prompt the IAU definition of a planet in 2006. Its moon Dysnomia orbits in 15.8 days.

discovery.by: Brown, M. E. et al. (Caltech, images 2004-12-28); Ortiz, J. L. et al. (Sierra Nevada, precovery 2003); credit disputed

haumea.summary: Haumea is a rapidly rotating (3.9 h), elongated dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt with two known moons (Hiʻiaka and Namaka) and a ring.

discovery.by: Brown, M. E., Trujillo, C. A., Rabinowitz, D.

makemake.summary: Makemake is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, among the brightest trans-Neptunian objects, with one known moon.

temperature.note: NSSDCA Small Worlds mean (-20 C); equatorial surface range 95-390 K
